recommendation: Keep the fix. It narrowly completes the published FHIR-18815 resolution; any future choice to forbid Bundle-local resolve() should be a new work-group decision because it would reverse the published issue text.
issue_request: FHIR-18815 was Published/Persuasive and asked FHIRPath Patch to clarify add behavior, mandatory insert index, missing-path errors except for delete, and the limit that FHIRPath must not refer outside the patched resource except for contained resources or Bundle-local resolution.
initial_application: The Jira comment GH#e04b204635 maps to git commit e04b204635956d32e6009669b760f411b43e2b00. That commit applied most rules to source/fhirpatch.html, including add, insert, delete, missing-path, sequencing, and a contained-resource resolve() restriction, but omitted the Jira-approved Bundle-local resolve() allowance.
additional_context: Later FHIRPath Patch page updates such as FHIR-34214 and FHIR-26324 did not revisit the resolve() scope rule. Current Bundle source defines reference resolution within Bundles, and fhirpatch.html is an active published page via publish.ini and source/hierarchy.xml. Community searches found no later conflicting FHIR-18815 decision.
reconciliation: Updated source/fhirpatch.html to prohibit resolve() from crossing outside the patched resource while expressly allowing contained resources and, when patching a Bundle, resources within that same Bundle. The server safety sentence now prohibits alterations outside the nominated target rather than accidentally excluding Bundle entries.
source_changes: source/fhirpatch.html: clarified the resolve() base rule and server safety sentence for Bundle-local resolution.

related_jiras.note: Current Bundle reference-resolution wording supports the same in-Bundle resolution model referenced by the FHIR-18815 Bundle exception.
Later FHIRPath Patch page cleanup confirmed the page remained active but did not revisit the FHIR-18815 resolve() rule.
Another FHIRPath Patch clarification already represented on the combined branch; it concerns move indexes, not the resolve() scope rule.
